entities.summary: The Precinct of Mut is an Ancient Egyptian temple compound located in the present city of Luxor, on the east bank of the Nile in South Karnak. The compound is one of the four key ancient temples that creates the Karnak Temple Complex. It is approximately 325 m (355 yd) south of the precinct of the god Amun. The precinct itself encompasses approximately 9 ha of the entire area. The Mut Precinct contains at least six temples: the Mut Temple, the Contra Temple, and Temples A, B, C, and D. Surrounding the Mut Temple proper, on three sides, is a sacred lake called the Isheru. Precinct of Mut is a archaeological site from Africa. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Precinct of Mut played a significant role in Ancient Egyptian religious practices and architecture, with its temples and surrounding lake influencing local culture for centuries. Its archaeological significance provides valuable insights into the history of Ancient Egypt.
